PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL - ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
REDLINE ANALYSIS MEMORANDUM: Cumulus Systems SaaS Agreement (markup returned Feb. 28, 2025)
To: Margaret Yuen, GC. From: Legal (for D. Kowalski). Reviewed: redline, template (Feb. 3, 2025), Playbook v3.0, Order Form OF-2025-0115-TG (OF), Kowalski email (Mar. 1, 2025).

1. BOTTOM LINE
- Cumulus's markup contains at least 15 Playbook Red positions (Section 3) and about 8 Yellow/Green. Playbook 1.4 triggers Clarendon & Finch (C&F) engagement at 3+ Reds; recommend authorizing it now (GC approval required, Playbook 15.1).
- Three compound Reds under Playbook 16: (a) data-breach exposure, (b) lock-in/exit, (c) SLA degradation.
- Cumulus's own executed Order Form contradicts its redline on escalator (3% hard cap, OF 3.2), 99.9% SLA and chronic-termination right (OF 5.2, "material terms"), and connector scope and 12-month warranty (OF 4.4). Lead with this; the Order Form controls on those subjects (OF 8.1).
- Do not sign as marked. Board re-approval is already triggered (3.7).

2. ERRORS AND GAPS IN THE MARCH 1 EMAIL (correct before positions harden)
- Connectors: the SOW (OF 4.4) lists Salesforce, ValveTrack MES and a 3PL Logistics connector, not SAP or Kronos.
- Contract value: $9.25M is flat 5 x $1.85M. At the OF's own 3% maximum, subscription is $9,821,901 plus $725,000 = $10,546,901, which already exceeds the $10.5M Board cap by $46,901. Playbook 6.1 says only "approaches."
- Escrow: Playbook 8.2 rates deletion without alternative Red, not Yellow; not a walk-away unless Cumulus also refuses a continuity alternative (then GC escalation).
- Assignment: the redline lets either party assign to an Affiliate without consent; the Red is the missing customer M&A carve-out, not consent "in any scenario."
- Governing law: the email calls Texas law "not necessarily a deal-breaker" but omits that venue moved to Travis County/W.D. Tex. and mediation to Austin. Law plus venue together is Red (Playbook 10.1).
- $15,000 "extraction fee": the redline makes standard export free; $15,000 is a minimum on uncapped hourly transition services.
- Omitted from the email: provider termination for convenience, IP sole-remedy, order-of-precedence reversal, entire-agreement supersession, expanded customer indemnity.
- Timing: Playbook 15.2 requires this memo within 5 business days of receipt (Mar. 7); the email says Mar. 14.
- Tracked changes: the redline's summary says 47 (19 material) and labels force majeure, mutual confidentiality and mediation "non-substantive"; XML holds about 170 insertion/133 deletion runs; 47 unverified.

3. PRIORITIZED ISSUES (Red = Playbook Red; GC approval needed to accept any Red; CFO Karen Aldrich also for liability, indemnity, insurance, escalator)
RED - TIER 1 (hold firm)
3.1 Liability cap (redline 9.1; JT-11). Vendor 2x ($3.7M) becomes one mutual cap of 12 months' fees "actually paid"; a competing "paid or payable" sentence sits directly beneath it (drafting conflict). Before the first payment (due about May 1, 2025) the cap could be near $0. All Excluded Claims (confidentiality, IP, data breach, gross negligence/willful misconduct) are struck, so the cap now covers gross negligence. 1x without 2x super-cap is Red (Playbook 2.1). Counter: restore 2x; fallback 1.5x only with super-caps; floor $1.85M plus 2x super-caps.
3.2 Consequential damages (9.2). All four carve-outs deleted; absolute exclusion is Playbook walk-away (2.2). Counter: restore all four; floor data breach and confidentiality.
3.3 Data-breach indemnity (10.2; no comment). The standalone vendor indemnity (notification, credit monitoring, regulatory fines) is replaced by a mutual "own negligence" indemnity expressly under the cap, with Customer now indemnifying Provider for its own negligence. Compound Red (Playbook 16 Ex. 1): maximum recovery is about $1.85M, no consequential damages, against about 2,200 employees' PII, valve designs, supplier pricing and SOX data. Cumulus disclosed an Aug. 2023 breach affecting 12 customers; SOC 2 Type II (Pinnacle, Dec. 15, 2024). The template is uncapped (9.1(c), 10.2(b)). Counter: open uncapped; authorized fallback 3x ($5.55M, Kowalski's proposal; Playbook preferred) with 2x ($3.7M) as floor, outside both cap and exclusion. Obtain the 2023 incident report and SOC 2 bridge letter; attach RFP security representations (supersession would erase them). Yes, hardest-held position.
3.4 Audit (11; JT-12). Paper review of SOC 2/ISO reports only; extra audits at Customer cost; template 11.5 regulatory-auditor access is gone. Red for SOX data (Playbook 7.4). Counter: fallback independent third-party audit scoped by Thorngate, unredacted results, 60-day remediation, post-incident audit, external-auditor access. SOC 2 is not an ICFR report; require a SOC 1 Type II. Playbook cites "AS 2201, formerly AS 2601"; PCAOB AS 2601 is the service-organization standard, so correct the citation.
3.5 Insurance (14.1). Cyber/E&O $10M to $3M; $5M umbrella deleted. Red (Playbook 9.1). $3M is below the 2x super-cap, so it cannot fund the indemnity. Counter $10M; fallback $5M cyber, $5M CGL, $3M umbrella; restore umbrella additional-insured status, 30-day cancellation notice, subrogation waiver (template 14.2).
3.6 Assignment and change of control (15.1-15.2). Consent required for Thorngate assignment "by operation of law"; vendor gets M&A carve-out; customer change-of-control termination deleted and replaced by notice only. Red on both (Playbook 11.1, 11.2). Counter: restore template 15.1/15.2 (fallback: mutual M&A and affiliate carve-out); restore 12.4 (fallback: competitor acquirer or adverse effect on performance). Frame as standard public-company M&A flexibility.
3.7 Fee escalator (3.2; JT-03). "Greater of 5% or CPI-U," with no ceiling and deemed acceptance after 30 days. Red (Playbook 6.1). Totals including $725,000 implementation: 3% $10,546,901; 5% $10,947,418 (+$447,418 over cap, matches email); 6% CPI about $11,153,622. Board re-approval is required before execution (Playbook 6.1, 15.1) and, since the 3% maximum already exceeds $10.5M, should be sought now. Counter: restore the 3% hard cap per OF 3.2; fallback lesser of CPI-U and 3%; delete deemed acceptance.
3.8 Termination for convenience (12.3). Deleted; replaced by 180 days' notice plus 75% of all remaining-term subscription fees, with no refund. Red (Playbook 5.1). After Year 1 at 3%: 75% x $7,971,901 = $5,978,926 (about $6.28M at 5%). Counter: restore; fallback after 24 months, or ETF capped at 25% of current-year remaining fees (example $231,250).
3.9 SLA (5.2, 5.3, Ex. B; JT-05, JT-06). 99.5% uptime (about 43.8 hours/year downtime vs 8.77); exclusions for 8 hours/month maintenance and third-party hosting outages (an express walk-away, Playbook 4.1); credits capped at 10% as sole remedy; chronic-underperformance exit deleted (98.5%); resolution targets "not guaranteed." Red (Playbook 4.2, 4.3; compound Ex. 3). Counter: 99.9% per OF 5.2 (fallback 99.7%, 4 hours maintenance with 48-hour notice, no hosting-provider exclusion); restore 15% tier and exit (fallback below 98.0% rolling 3 months or 97.5% in one month); keep credits from limiting termination (template 5.3).
3.10 Data portability and deletion (7.4, 7.5; JT-08, JT-09). 90-day return in "Provider's then-standard format"; services at uncapped rates with $15,000 minimum; deletion 60 to 180 days. Red (return over 60 days; proprietary format; Playbook 7.2). Aggregated Data retained in perpetuity and defined as not Customer Data: Red because the data includes trade secrets (Playbook 7.3). Sequence trap: access ends at termination, export arrives up to day 90, but deletion must be requested within 30 days. Counter: 30 days (fallback 45), CSV/XML/JSON/SQL, free export, migration help capped at $10,000, read-only access during transition, Playbook 7.3 (a)-(d) conditions or delete Aggregated Data, deletion within 60 days with NIST SP 800-88.
3.11 Integration warranty (6.3; JT-07; Ex. A). "AS IS" for all connectors and interoperability with existing systems. Red (Playbook 12.2) because it contradicts OF 4.4 (in-scope deliverables, no extra fees, 12-month warranty). Restore template 4.2, 6.2(f), 6.4; strike the new Ex. A Agreement-controls line.
3.12 Source code escrow (8.5; JT-10). Deleted, no alternative. Red (Playbook 8.2). Counter: "technology escrow" (documentation, API specs, schemas, deployment scripts, data dictionary), same release triggers, 90-day transition plan, and cooperation on release (Playbook fallback); or step-in/last-resort license. JT-10 itself offers "step-in rights"; use it.
3.13 Governing law (16.1-16.3). Texas law, Travis County/W.D. Tex. exclusive venue, mediation in Austin: Red. Counter Ohio/Summit County; fallback Delaware or neutral venue. Mediation text references arbitration though none exists; fix.
3.14 Term and renewal (12.1, new provider termination). Auto-renewal with 180-day notice (first deadline Oct. 2, 2029) is Red (over 120 days); it conflicts with OF 2.2 (renewal by mutual agreement). New unflagged Provider right to terminate for convenience on 12 months' notice is not in the Playbook; treat as Red for an ERP. Counter: opt-in renewal (fallback 90 days, capped escalator); delete the provider right or limit it to post-Initial Term with 24 months' notice. Compound Ex. 2 lock-in applies with 3.8 and 3.10.
3.15 IP indemnity (10.1). Sole remedy with refund of prepaid subscription fees only (no implementation fees) is Red (Playbook 3.1); exclusion for combinations with non-Provider products could swallow the SOW integrations. Restore template 10.1(b), (c) (includes one year's fee) and (d) integration clarification. Vendor violation-of-law indemnity (template 10.3) is missing from the markup base: Red if deleted (Playbook 3.3).
YELLOW / GREEN
3.16 Force majeure (1.10, 13) adds pandemic and "cyber attack on third-party infrastructure": Yellow (Playbook 14); limit to attacks not preventable by required controls. Payment carve-out and 90-day exit preserved.
3.17 Warranty remedy (6.3): sole remedy, 60-day cure, pro-rata refund only: Yellow; restore 30 days and implementation-fee refund.
3.18 Mutual confidentiality (4): Green; restore "Customer Data is Confidential Information in all circumstances."
3.19 Fees: "non-cancellable/non-refundable" (3.1): Yellow ("except as provided"); 60-day payment cure and 1.5% interest: Green; suspension after 45 days: add good-faith-dispute carve-out (template 3.6).
3.20 Customer indemnity expanded ("breach of applicable law"): Yellow, delete.
3.21 Feedback license (8.3): Yellow; exclude Customer Data. Service-bureau ban: confirm Affiliates not caught. Publicity (17.9) approval-gated and construction clause: Green. Survival list omits 7.4, 8.5 and insurance tail: Yellow. "Customer and its Affiliates": Yellow. Breach notice 72 hours (7.3, DPA 4; OF 6.2 also 72): at Playbook Red threshold edge; template said 48; restore 48 (fallback 48 per Playbook 13).

4. INTERACTION EFFECTS (Playbook 16 - required section)
- Data breach: cap (3.1) + exclusion (3.2) + indemnity (3.3) + $3M insurance (3.5) = Red; maximum recovery about $1.85M against potential eight-figure loss.
- Lock-in: no convenience exit (3.8) + 90-day proprietary export (3.10) + auto-renewal (3.14) + no escrow (3.12) + provider walk-away right = Red.
- SLA: 99.5%, hosting exclusions, credit cap and no exit (3.9) = Red.
- Precedence: the Agreement-controls sentence, Ex. A statement and entire-agreement supersession could nullify the OF's 3% cap, 99.9% SLA, connector scope and warranty. Template 17.10 lets an order form prevail only if it names the superseded provision; OF 8.1 does not, so conform the Agreement to the OF.
- Untracked drift: the markup's base text does not match the Feb. 3 template. Unmarked omissions include template 6.2(c),(e),(g), 7.2 (no benchmarking/AI use), 7.7, 10.3, 11.3/11.5, 14.2(b), 16.3/16.4 and 5.5 (72-hour notice, 4-hour maintenance). Run a full machine comparison and demand conformed text.

5. AUTHORITY, ESCALATION AND STRATEGY
- Approvals: GC for every Red; CFO co-approval for items 3.1, 3.3, 3.5, 3.7; Board re-approval (spend over $10.5M, Playbook 15.1); Audit Committee briefing for audit rights (15.2). OF signed by the VP of IT; our copy shows blank signature lines. Confirm execution, authority under the June 2024 Delegation of Authority, and Board visibility, since TCV exceeds $10M.
- Sequence: send a Tier 1 package first (3.1-3.4, 3.6-3.9); concede Greens and "Provider" terminology. Trade 99.7% or 24-month TfC only for the breach package and escrow alternative. Year 1 fee is payable from April 1 regardless of go-live (OF 2.1); do not let schedule pressure from B. Hargrove or Ridgeline weaken Tier 1. Share only a sanitized summary with the business team and Ridgeline; the Playbook and this memo are privileged and must not go to third-party consultants.
- Outside counsel: engage C&F now, including Texas-law review (Playbook 10.1) of cap and gross-negligence enforceability (unverified).

6. GC-ONLY RESTRICTED NOTE (strip from any shared copy)
Ferriston discussions: consistent with the email, nothing about them should appear in negotiations or business communications (also an MNPI/insider-list matter for a NASDAQ issuer). Frame 3.6 solely as standard public-company M&A flexibility (Playbook 11.1). Affiliate-assignment carve-out helps only post-closing; do not rely on it. Contacting Ferriston or its advisers about this contract is a GC decision; I recommend against it now. C&F's prior Ferriston NDA work supports using it within the need-to-know group.
